designSummary: Cohort of first discharges per child; time to first asthma emergency revisit or readmission within 90 days; complete versus incomplete plan.
sampleSize: About 620 asthma admissions a year give about 2,480 discharges over four years and about 1,900 first discharges per child. With a 16 percent 90-day revisit risk, about 300 events are expected. If 45 percent of plans are complete, 300 events give 80 percent power at two-sided alpha 0.05 to detect a hazard ratio of about 0.72 (Schoenfeld approximation); a hazard ratio of 0.80 would need about 640 events, roughly eight years of discharges. The estimate will be reported with its confidence interval, not as a significance verdict.
primaryAnalysis: Cox model for time to first asthma emergency revisit or readmission within 90 days, adjusted for the seven pre-specified covariates, with robust standard errors; proportional hazards checked with scaled Schoenfeld residuals.
secondaryAnalysis: The same model for 90-day readmission and 30-day revisit; the negative control outcome; the association by caregiver language preference as a pre-specified interaction (h2); item-level completeness described without testing.
missingData: Plans missing from the scan archive are reported and treated as not assessed, never as incomplete; covariates missing for more than 5 percent of children are handled by multiple imputation with 20 imputations; children who move out of the province are censored at the last provincial contact.
multiplicity: One primary contrast; secondary outcomes and the language interaction are labelled as secondary and reported with confidence intervals only.
software: R with the survival package; code and covariate list archived before the linked file is received.
overfittingGuards: About 40 events per covariate for the primary model
summary: About 300 expected events give 80 percent power for a hazard ratio of about 0.72; smaller effects would need more years of discharges.
